Subject: Operational affirmation: VM scan tempo, SLAs, and patch escalation matrix

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. AcmePay's external auditor has asked us to get a concise operational statement on your vulnerability management rhythm ahead of next week's SOC 2 Readiness call. Specifically they want:

- Scan cadence by asset class (internet-facing, internal infra, containers, third-party libs).
- SLA targets for CVE handling by severity (what you commit to and how you measure it).
- Definition of "mitigation" vs "remediation" in practice.
- Escalation/ownership matrix when fixes miss SLA windows.
- A sample index or manifest showing recent scan runs and timestamps for verification.

Can you provide a short, operational confirmation and any artifacts you can share (redacted manifest or index is fine)? If you have a single-file matrix we can attach to the auditor packet that would be ideal.

Also please include who our procurement/audit liaison should contact if there are contract or SLA exceptions.

Samuel Park
Security Program Manager
AcmePay

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational affirmation: VM scan tempo, SLAs, and patch escalation matrix

Samuel —

Appreciate the clear ask. Below is an operational summary that you can include in the auditor packet. I will also attach the scan index and our escalation matrix as requested. Let me know if you want this signed/declared on Redwood letterhead; we can route that through legal.

Operational summary (short):

- Scan cadence (by asset class):
  • Internet-facing hosts / LB frontends: authenticated daily + unauthenticated daily
  • Internal hosts (prod control plane): authenticated weekly
  • Containers (registry images): CI/CD image-scanning on build + nightly registry sweep
  • Third-party library/OSS inventory: weekly SBOM-driven scanning, monthly deep dependency analysis

- SLA targets (time-to-mitigate / remediate measured from initial detection):
  • Critical (CVSS 9.0-10.0 or exploit in active use): 48 hours to mitigation (isolate/workaround), 14 days to verified remediation where possible
  • High (CVSS 7.0-8.9): 7 days to mitigation, 30 days to remediation
  • Medium (CVSS 4.0-6.9): 30 days to remediation cadence
  • Low (<4.0): 90 days or aligned with routine maintenance windows

- Mitigation vs remediation (short):
  • Mitigation — temporary controls to reduce risk (network ACLs, WAF rules, instance isolation, disabling vulnerable feature).
  • Remediation — permanent fix (patch, upgrade, configuration change) with verification via follow-up scan and regression checks.

- Escalation & ownership matrix:
  1) Automated triage assigns owner in Jira within 2 hours of detection.
  2) If SLA for mitigation is missed, incident is auto-escalated to on-call manager and Security Ops within 24 hours.
  3) If remediation timeline is at risk, the Engineering Manager and Product Security engage in a weekly remediation stand-up; for Critical items an emergency patch window is triggered.

- Exceptions & third-party dependencies:
  • When remediation depends on a vendor patch (third-party component), we commit to compensating controls within 48 hours and weekly status until vendor fix is applied.

Attachments included: vm-scan-index.csv (last 30 days scan timestamps, asset classes), cve-escalation-matrix.pdf (matrix with owners and on-call contacts).

Procurement/audit liaison: procurement@redwood.com (primary), legal@redwood.com (for SLA redlines).

Next step: please confirm acceptance or list any requested exceptions and we will produce a one-page letter and the artifacts for your auditor.

—Jonas Weber
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Samuel —

Answers inline below and a short sample timeline attached. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if the auditor needs live walk-through.

1) SLA clock: calendar hours. We measure from detection timestamp in our scanner to the mitigation action timestamp in our ticketing system. For Critical items that clock is 48 calendar hours.

2) Vendor exceptions: yes — when remediation depends on a third-party vendor we open a vendor-support ticket and record the vendor ticket ID in our Jira remediation ticket (field: vendor_reference). We include that ticket id in the weekly status exports so auditors can trace the vendor engagement.

3) Sample timeline (redacted):
  • Detection: 2028-06-11T02:13:47Z (internal registry image scan identified CVE-2028-1145)
  • Mitigation: 2028-06-11T18:02:09Z (image quarantined and runtime limit applied)
  • Vendor patch release: 2028-06-13T11:04:00Z (vendor released patched base image)
  • Remediation: 2028-06-14T03:22:30Z (image rebuilt and deployed to canary, follow-up scans negative)
  • Verification: 2028-06-14T06:40:05Z (regression scan passed and ticket closed)

Attached is a redacted single-page timeline called "critical-cve-sample-timeline.pdf" and the same entries are included in the vm-scan-index CSV we sent. For SOC 2 purposes we also maintain a signed runbook; if the auditor requires a letter on company letterhead, indicate that and legal will prepare it.

Escalation contact (if you need an executive sign-off):
  • Marissa Cole, VP Security Programs — marissa.cole@redwood.com
  • Procurement contact for SLA redlines: procurement@redwood.com

Best,

Kimberly Park
